#!/bin/sh
# The one command that makes build.nbt from scratch: the parts, then the roof check, then into place.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
MCD="node /Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/bin/mcd.mjs"
TMP="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/villa-build.$$.nbt"          # .nbt: the toolkit picks the format by extension
trap 'rm -f "$TMP"' EXIT

node build.mjs "$TMP"

# the roof step (plan.md ROOFS): dry run first; skipped while the shell is still a stub (no walls to roof)
if grep -q '^// STUB' parts/shell.mjs; then
  echo "roof: skipped (shell is still a stub)"
else
  $MCD roof "$TMP" --dry-run --style shed
fi

mv "$TMP" build.nbt
$MCD info build.nbt
---
// villa-haiku part 4: the atrium's centre. The rain pool (impluvium) under the compluvium, the four standing lamps at the
// atrium corners, and the potted plants at the peristyle walkway ends. Nothing goes over the pool or the doorways.
// Ticks E04 E05 E20 E21.
import { ATRIUM_LAMPS, IMPLUVIUM, WALKWAY_POTS, impluvium, lamp, pot } from "../vocab.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  impluvium(g, IMPLUVIUM);
  for (const [x, z] of ATRIUM_LAMPS) lamp(g, x, z);
  WALKWAY_POTS.forEach(([x, z], i) => pot(g, x, z, i % 2 ? "azalea" : "fern"));
}
---
